name: mil-txt
description: Automatically execute to-do items from a Markdown/text file (checkbox tasks) — the text-file analogue of /mil, which iterates a minflow deck. Reads the file at $1, executes the top unchecked task, flips it to done, updates the Notes/Done sections, and loops.

b0000002-get-4000-8000-000000000002.name: GET TOP TASK
b0000002-get-4000-8000-000000000002.prompt:
[Automated flowchart step — not a user message.]

You are iterating a Markdown to-do file. The file path is: $1

Read that file. Its shape is:
# <title>
## Notes
<notes>
## Done
<done>
## Tasks
- [ ] an incomplete task
- [x] a completed task

Find the FIRST unchecked task line (matching `- [ ]`) in the `## Tasks` section — that is the top card.

Return structured output:
- has_card: true if an unchecked `- [ ]` task exists, false if none remain
- card_text: the task text with the leading `- [ ] ` removed (empty if has_card is false)
- todo_path: the exact file path you were given ($1)
- deck_description: the file's title (the `# ...` line)
- deck_done: the contents of the `## Done` section
- deck_notes: the contents of the `## Notes` section

Do NOT modify the file in this step.

b0000004-exec-4000-8000-000000000004.name: EXECUTE TASK

b0000005-chk-4000-8000-000000000005.name: CHECK APPROVAL
b0000005-chk-4000-8000-000000000005.prompt:
[Automated flowchart step — not a user message.]

You just worked on: {{card_text}}

Determine whether this work can be automatically marked complete, or whether it requires human review/approval.

Default to auto-completing. Only require approval in these cases:
- Plan tasks: require approval ONLY if the plan involves very complex architecture or genuinely ambiguous requirements where you could easily go the wrong direction. Straightforward plans should auto-complete.
- Research tasks: auto-complete UNLESS you uncovered something highly pertinent that the user would want to act on immediately (e.g. a critical finding, a decision point, something that changes project direction). Routine research summaries auto-complete.
- Failed or incomplete work: ALWAYS requires approval

Always auto-complete in these cases:
- Task restructuring/splitting: if you split the task into sub-tasks, auto-complete. The restructuring IS the completed work — sub-tasks will execute in subsequent iterations.
- Gate/verification tasks with headless-verified assertions: if all assertions have passing automated tests and you have documented reasons for not live-testing specific ones, auto-complete with a gap note.

Everything else (implementation, testing, git operations, etc.) should auto-complete.

Bias strongly toward auto-completing. The user wants momentum, not gatekeeping.

b0000007-mark-4000-8000-000000000007.name: MARK COMPLETE
b0000007-mark-4000-8000-000000000007.prompt:
[Automated flowchart step — output goes to the user.]

Mark the task complete in the file {{todo_path}}: use Edit to change the FIRST line that reads exactly `- [ ] {{card_text}}` into `- [x] {{card_text}}` — flip the checkbox only, change nothing else on the line. If several lines match identically, change only the first.

Then briefly confirm to the user that "{{card_text}}" has been auto-completed.

b0000010-updk-4000-8000-000000000010.name: UPDATE NOTES
b0000010-updk-4000-8000-000000000010.prompt:
[Automated flowchart step — not a user message.]

You just completed: {{card_text}}

Update the to-do file's narrative sections with Edit on {{todo_path}}:

1. `## Done` — append what was just completed to the existing summary.
2. `## Notes` — refresh with current project state (open questions, blockers, active context); remove stale info.

Keep both fields concise. The `## Done` section is a running summary of completed milestones; `## Notes` is current context. Do not touch the `## Tasks` list here.

Do not output any text to the user.

b0000009-noti-4000-8000-000000000009.name: NOTIFY USER
b0000009-noti-4000-8000-000000000009.prompt:
[Automated flowchart step — output goes to the user.]

The work on "{{card_text}}" requires human review before it can be marked complete.

Reason: {{reason}}

Send a clear, concise summary to the user explaining:
1. What was accomplished
2. Why human review is needed
3. What specifically they should review or verify

b000000g-proc-4000-8000-00000000000g.name: PROCESS RESPONSE
b000000g-proc-4000-8000-00000000000g.prompt:
[Automated flowchart step — output goes to the user.]

You were working on: {{card_text}}

The user responded: {{user_response}}

Act on the user's response. This could be:
- Approval to continue ("go", "approved", "yes", etc.) — acknowledge briefly
- A direction or instruction — follow it, then confirm what you did
- A question — answer it

After handling the response, the task will be marked complete and /mil-txt will continue to the next task.

b000000c-chkt-4000-8000-00000000000c.name: CHECK MANUAL TEST
b000000c-chkt-4000-8000-00000000000c.prompt:
[Automated flowchart step — not a user message.]

Review the work completed during this /mil-txt session. Was any code, configuration, or functionality implemented or changed?

Set needs_test to true if something was implemented that the user should manually verify. Set to false if the session only did planning, research, documentation, or git operations with no functional changes.

b000000e-addt-4000-8000-00000000000e.name: ADD TEST TASK
b000000e-addt-4000-8000-00000000000e.prompt:
[Automated flowchart step — output goes to the user.]

Add a manual-testing task to the to-do file: use Edit on {{todo_path}} to insert the line `- [ ] Manually test changes` at the TOP of the `## Tasks` section.

Then list the specific changes that require manual testing. For each change, state:
- What was changed
- What the user should do to test it (specific steps)
- What a successful test looks like

Be brief — use bullet points.
